source_excerpts.text:
## 5. The complete resource bill and the executed receiver

The construction has an explicit positive floor. Let

\[
q=\left\|\sum_jL_j^\dagger L_j\right\|.
\]

The source’s no-jump term gives, throughout \(0\le t\le T\),

\[
\rho_t\ge\mu I,
\qquad
\mu=\frac{\epsilon e^{-qT}}{d^2}.
\]

If a faithful stationary state \(\sigma\) is known, the stronger bound

\[
\mu=\frac{\epsilon}{d^2\kappa(\sigma)}
\]

holds uniformly in \(T\). For a unital source, \(\mu=\epsilon/d^2\).

Writing \(g=\|G\|\), \(l_j=\|L_j\|\),
\(s=\sum_jl_j^2\), and \(b=2g+s\), the report proves

\[
\|C_j\|\le l_j\mu^{-1/2},
\qquad
\|H_M\|\le g\mu^{-1/2},
\]

and

\[
\|\dot C_j\|\le l_jb\mu^{-3/2},
\qquad
\|\dot H_M\|\le gb\mu^{-3/2}.
\]

Linear interpolation of finitely many control matrices provides finite slew. A sufficient number of intervals for control error \(\zeta\) is

\[
N\ge
\frac{2b(g+5s)T^2}{\zeta\mu^2}.
\]

Finite turn-on and turn-off ramps have their own error budget. Coefficient uncertainty, calibration error and terminal local gates are priced separately.

At fixed source and horizon, a target collection error \(\delta\) can be obtained with peak strengths \(O(\delta^{-1})\) and a conservative program length \(O(\delta^{-5})\). These are sufficient bounds, not optimized ones. Dense control storage scales as \(O(N(m+1)d^4)\), and dense matrix calculations involve \(O(d^6)\) operations per root or Sylvester solve.

Thus \(d^2\) receiver levels do not imply an efficient construction in the number \(\log d\) of source qubits. Nor do bounded Markov coefficients bound a full microscopic system–field Hamiltonian.

statement: A finite positive floor gives finite controls,not a fixed-hardware or efficient-in-log-d guarantee.
